subject: Short-term throughput expansion + reconciled overrun proposal
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Patel <maya@scaleops.com>, scaleops-support@scaleops.com
Cc: 
Date: 2025-05-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Capacity increase request: temporary throughput for launch

Maya —

Congrats on the upcoming marketing launch. We saw ScaleOps spike against the current quota this morning and I wanted to propose a short-term throughput expansion to cover the next three weeks. High level:

- Request: +2.5x burst headroom for 21 days (global).
- Why: expected traffic during campaign window will push concurrency and token volumes beyond committed QPS.
- Ask: please confirm whether procurement would prefer a PO for a one-time uplift or a reconciled true-up invoice after the window.

To make decisions easier, I attached a quick proposal with two paths: a prorated uplift charge vs. converting last month's overrun into a temporary committed buffer with a discounted add-on. See attached: ephemeral_proposal_v1.pdf (1 page).

If you can share the PO cadence and an initial acceptance by EOD tomorrow we can schedule the capacity changes for Friday.

Thanks —
Sergio Alvarez
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
attachment: ephemeral_proposal_v1.pdf (pdf)
From: Maya Patel <maya@scaleops.com>

Cc: scaleops-support@scaleops.com
Date: 2025-05-21T12:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity increase request: temporary throughput for launch

Sergio —

Thanks for the heads up and the one-pager. We definitely need extra headroom for the launch (creative has been approved and the spike is expected next week). A few quick items from procurement:

- We prefer a PO-backed change if the uplift is > $5K. Otherwise, procurement will accept a reconciled invoice.
- Can you provide a prorated quote for the 21-day uplift and a separate true-up number for last month's overrun? Procurement also needs an estimated effective date for the uplift to align the PO.
- Our legal team will want a one-line amendment or SOW addendum for the temporary increase (no full contract change).

I can loop in procurement formally once we have the numbers. If you have a mutual action plan (dates + owner + deliverables) that would speed things up.

— Maya
Maya Patel
Head of Platform, ScaleOps
maya@scaleops.com
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: 2025-05-21T14:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity increase request: temporary throughput for launch — pricing options

Sergio / Laura —

I ran the numbers against ScaleOps' recent usage and the proposed +2.5x for 21 days. Two clean options to present:

Option A — Prorated Uplift (no commitment conversion)
- Short-term uplift for 21 days at blended uplift rate = $0.0095 per token-equivalent
- Estimated uplift invoice (prorated) = $4,350
- No contractual change; one-off invoice after window.

Option B — Temporary Buffer + Reconciled True-Up (preferred)
- Convert last month's 18% overrun into a 21-day committed buffer. Apply a 10% concession on uplift consumption for the buffer period as goodwill.
- One-time reconciled true-up to close prior overrun = $3,900.
- 21-day buffer cost (after concession) = $3,150.
- Net ask this period (true-up + buffer) = $7,050, but we can split to: 60% invoice now / 40% post-window to ease PO cadence.

Rationale for Option B: reduces surprise billing sensitivity, gives customer predictable headroom, and keeps renewal economics healthier.

If procurement needs a PO threshold change we can lower the upfront by amortizing the post-window portion to the next invoice. Attached is the calc sheet (pricing_calc_sheet.csv) with line-by-line token assumptions.

— Jordan
Sales Operations, Redwood Inference

Maya —

Following up with a concise proposal based on Jordan's calc:

Recommended path (Option B, streamlined):
1) Immediate: standby the 21-day burst (start Friday 2025-05-23 00:00 UTC).
2) Billing: 60% of net ($4,230) payable via PO / invoice now; remaining 40% ($2,820) invoiced after the window as reconciled true-up.
3) Contract: SOW addendum (1 line) to document the temporary headroom + reconciliation terms. Minimal legal review expected.
4) Next steps: Maya to confirm procurement's PO cadence; Laura to prepare the one-line SOW addendum draft; Jordan will generate the exact invoice numbers and DocuSign link.

DocuSign (proposal): https://docusign.example.com/ntf-SCL-4821
Drive (detailed calcs): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-scaleops-burst-proposal

If that flow works for ScaleOps I can mark the change and schedule engineers to provision the buffer Friday morning.
